name: East Gardens of the Imperial Palace
about: The East Gardens occupy part of the former Edo Castle grounds and are open to the public free of charge. Visitors walk among stone foundations, moats and guardhouses, and through a large lawn and a Japanese garden. Entry is through the Otemon, Hirakawa or Kitahanebashi gates. Opening hours change with the season, and the garden is closed on Mondays and Fridays.
hours: 9:00-16:00 (Nov-Feb); Mar 1-Apr 14 9:00-17:00; Apr 15-Aug 9:00-18:00; Sep 9:00-17:00; Oct 9:00-16:30. Last entry 30 minutes before closing (check the official page for exact seasonal rules)
closed: Mondays and Fridays; Dec 28-Jan 3; days with events
station: Otemachi Station (Chiyoda, Tozai, Marunouchi, Hanzomon, Toei Mita Lines)
car: Not practical; public transport is easier

name: Tokyo National Museum
about: Japan's oldest museum, founded in 1872 and located in Ueno Park. Its collection covers Japanese art and archaeology, including samurai swords, kimono, ceramics and Buddhist sculpture, along with works from other parts of Asia. The main exhibits are spread across several buildings, so choosing one or two is easier than trying to see everything. Special exhibitions are ticketed separately.
hours: 9:30-17:00 (until 20:00 on Fridays and Saturdays at times); last entry 30 minutes before closing
closed: Mondays (open if a national holiday, closed the next day); Dec 26-31 in 2026
price: Permanent exhibits: adults 1,000 yen, university students 500 yen; free for under 18 and 70 and over with proof of age. Special exhibitions cost extra
station: Ueno Station (JR lines) or Uguisudani Station (JR Yamanote Line)
car: Not recommended; public transport is easier

name: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
name_ja: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
about: A museum dedicated to the work of Studio Ghibli, set in a small park west of central Tokyo. Rooms display original drawings and animation tools, and there is a short film shown only at the museum. Entry is only with a ticket bought in advance, and tickets are not sold at the door. Photography inside is not allowed.
closed: Usually Tuesdays; also around year-end and for maintenance (check the official calendar)
price: Adults about 1,000 yen. Tickets must be bought in advance online; none are sold at the museum
car: Not possible; the museum asks visitors to use public transport

name: Zojoji Temple
about: A Jodo sect temple founded in 1393 and moved to its present site in 1598. It became the family temple of the Tokugawa shoguns, and six of the shoguns are buried here. The grounds are free to enter and Tokyo Tower stands directly behind the main hall. The Sangedatsumon gate dates from 1622 and is among the oldest wooden structures in Tokyo. A Treasures Gallery in the main hall basement and the Tokugawa graveyard are open for a fee.
hours: Grounds about 9:00-17:00; Treasures Gallery weekdays 11:00-15:00, weekends and holidays 10:00-16:00
closed: Treasures Gallery closed Tuesdays (unless a national holiday)
price: Grounds free; Treasures Gallery adults 700 yen, junior and senior high 300 yen; combined ticket with the Tokugawa graveyard 1,000 yen
parking: Ask the temple; visitors are asked to use public transport
car: Possible, but the temple asks visitors to use public transport

name: Tokyo Metropolitan Edo-Tokyo Museum
name_ja: 東京都江戸東京博物館
about: A history museum covering Edo and Tokyo from the early 1600s to the present. It closed for about four years for renovation and reopened on 31 March 2026. The permanent galleries include full-scale and model buildings, townscapes and everyday objects. Special exhibitions are priced separately. Check the official site for current hours before visiting.
hours: 9:30-17:30 (Saturdays until 19:30); last entry 30 minutes before closing
closed: Mondays (open if a national holiday, closed the next day); New Year holidays
price: Permanent exhibition: adults 800 yen; free for junior high school age and under. Special exhibitions cost extra
station: Ryogoku Station (Toei Oedo Line, JR Sobu Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Kabukiza Theatre
about: Tokyo's main kabuki theatre, run by Shochiku, with 1,808 seats plus standing and single-act seats. The current building was completed in 2013 and was designed with Kengo Kuma and Associates. Full programs run several hours. Single-act tickets (makumi) let visitors watch one act and are sold on the day at the theatre, so they suit first-time visitors. English audio guides are available at many performances. Check the official schedule for performance dates.
hours: Depends on the performance schedule; single-act tickets go on sale shortly before each act
price: Full-program tickets about 4,000-20,000 yen; single-act tickets are cheaper (roughly 1,000-2,000 yen, varies by act)
station: Higashi-Ginza Station (Hibiya Line, Toei Asakusa Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Yanaka Ginza
about: A short shopping street of about 170 metres lined with roughly 60 small shops, in one of the older residential districts of Tokyo. Shops sell fresh and prepared food, tea and Japanese sweets, and many are family run. Street food such as croquettes and skewers is easy to eat while walking. At the west end the Yuyake Dandan stairway gives a view down the street. Cat-themed goods are a local theme.
hours: Varies by shop; most shops close in the early evening
price: Free to walk; snacks from a few hundred yen each
station: Nippori Station (JR lines, Keisei Line, Nippori-Toneri Liner)
parking: No street parking; paid parking nearby
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Gotokuji Temple
about: A Soto Zen temple in a quiet residential part of Setagaya. It is known as a place linked to the origin of the maneki-neko, the beckoning cat figure, according to local tradition. Small white cat figurines are offered in rows at a dedicated spot in the grounds. Figurines can be bought at the temple office. Visitors are asked not to write on the figurines.
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Asakusa Kagetsudo (Main Store)
name_ja: 浅草 花月堂 本店
about: A melon pan bakery near Asakusa's Sensoji area, known for its jumbo melon pan. The bread is baked through the day and sold fresh and warm. It closes when the day's batch sells out. Most people take it away.
hours: Weekdays from 11:00, weekends and holidays from 10:00, until sold out
station: Asakusa Station (Ginza Line, Asakusa Line, Tsukuba Express)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Shiseido Parlour Ginza Main Store (Salon de Café)
name_ja: 資生堂パーラー 銀座本店 サロン・ド・カフェ
about: The Salon de Café on the 3rd floor of the Tokyo Ginza Shiseido Building, run by Shiseido Parlour, which has operated in Ginza since the early 20th century. The cafe serves cakes, parfaits and light meals, including seasonal parfaits. The upstairs restaurant on higher floors serves full meals such as omelette rice and beef stew.
price: Parfaits and cakes with a drink from about 2,000 yen (varies)
station: Shimbashi Station (JR lines, Ginza Line, Asakusa Line) or Ginza Station (Ginza, Marunouchi, Hibiya Lines)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Kayaba Coffee
about: A coffee shop in a wooden building dating from 1916, operating as Kayaba Coffee since 1938 and reopened after renovation. It is in the Yanaka district, near Nippori. Egg sandwiches are a signature item, along with coffee and desserts. Check its current hours before visiting.
price: Egg sandwich about 1,000 yen; coffee extra
station: Nezu Station (Chiyoda Line) or Nippori Station (JR lines)
car: Not practical; public transport is easier

name: Blue Bottle Coffee Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Flagship Cafe
name_ja: ブルーボトルコーヒー 清澄白河フラッグシップカフェ
about: The first Blue Bottle Coffee location opened outside the United States, in a converted warehouse in the Kiyosumi-Shirakawa area. It opened in February 2015 and was later reopened as a flagship. The cafe serves drip coffee, espresso drinks and food. The neighbourhood has other coffee shops and the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo nearby.
closed: Open daily (closed for the New Year holiday)
station: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Station (Hanzomon Line, Toei Oedo Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Toraya Akasaka Store (and Toraya Cafe)
about: The main store of Toraya, a traditional Japanese confectioner, with a tea room attached. Toraya sells yokan (sweet bean jelly) and other wagashi. The tea room serves seasonal wagashi, anmitsu and tea. A yokan flavour called Senri no Kaze is sold only at this store.
hours: Store: weekdays 9:00-18:00, weekends and holidays 9:30-18:00; tea room about 11:00-17:30 (last order 17:00; may have changed)
closed: Reported as the 6th of each month (Jan-Nov); confirm by phone or on the official site
price: Anmitsu set with a drink 2,750 yen

name: Fuglen Tokyo
name_ja: フグレン トウキョウ
about: A coffee shop in Tomigaya with a Norwegian background, serving light-roast coffee in a Scandinavian vintage setting. It is a short walk from Yoyogi Park. The daytime menu is coffee and light food. The room changes to a bar in the evening. Opening hours vary by day.
hours: Varies by day, from about 7:00 until late evening (check before visiting)
car: Not practical; public transport is easier

name: Glitch Coffee & Roasters
name_ja: グリッチ コーヒー＆ロースターズ
about: A specialty coffee shop and roaster near Jimbocho, an area known for second-hand bookshops. It serves hand-brewed filter coffee made from single-origin beans. Many visitors combine it with a walk through the nearby book streets. Hours are slightly different on weekdays and weekends.
closed: No scheduled holidays listed (confirm on social media)
station: Jimbocho Station (Hanzomon Line, Toei Mita Line, Toei Shinjuku Line)
car: Not practical; public transport is easier

name: Marion Crêpes (Harajuku Takeshita Street)
name_ja: マリオンクレープ 原宿竹下通り店
about: A crêpe stand on Takeshita Street, which has sold crêpes since the 1970s and is often credited with starting Harajuku's crêpe culture. Crêpes are made to order and eaten as takeaway, with sweet fillings such as cream and fruit and some savoury options. The street is very crowded on weekends and holidays.
car: Not practical; public transport is easier

name: Café de l'Ambre
name_ja: カフェ・ド・ランブル
about: A coffee shop in Ginza, opened in 1948 by Ichiro Sekiguchi, who died in 2018 at age 103. It specialises in aged coffee beans, some stored for many years, and serves them as drip coffee. The shop continues under staff he trained. It is a small, old-style kissaten, and coffee is the focus rather than food.
station: Shimbashi Station (JR lines, Ginza Line, Asakusa Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Sakurai Japanese Tea Experience
name_ja: 櫻井焙茶研究所 / SAKURAI TEA EXPERIENCE
about: A tea room on the 5th floor of the Spiral building in Minami-Aoyama. Guests sit at a counter and are served Japanese teas chosen and prepared for them, with a small sweet. The room has about eight counter seats, so booking ahead is recommended. In the evening it operates as a bar with a cover charge.
hours: Weekdays 11:00-19:00; weekends and holidays 11:00-20:00 (last order 19:00); bar time weekdays 19:00-23:00
price: Seat-only booking 2,500 yen per person; tea courses cost more (confirm when booking)
station: Omotesando Station (Ginza Line, Chiyoda Line, Hanzomon Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier
